source_evidence: docs/GRAMMAR_STRATEGY.md §§3b and 4 (structured input; form is the only cue to meaning)
docs/research/error-profiles/fr.md §§2.10 and 6 (15 recorded passé-composé/imparfait selection errors; keep the target small)
_meta.provenance: Fifty newly authored, bank-attested seed items in standard French; no learner sentences or personal data are reproduced.
_meta.language_policy: sentence, question, options, answer, and contrast_form are French; why is concise English metalinguistic feedback.
_meta.validation_notes: Every frame occurs once in each tense. Apart from grammatically required auxiliary, participle, agreement, and je/j' elision, each contrast changes only target verbal morphology. No time adverb, duration phrase, habitual-frequency expression, completion predicate, or surrounding event independently supplies the aspect reading. Passé composé is described as bounded/perfective, not as proof that every real-world consequence is complete; imparfait is described as an internal/background view without an asserted endpoint.
